'''Paul Rudolf Eugen Jahnke''' (November 30, 1861, in Berlin – October 18, 1921, in Berlin) was a German [[mathematician]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Anonymous |title=Eugen Jahnke |journal=Dinglers Polytechnisches Journal |date=5 November 1921 |volume=336 |issue=22 |page=313 |url=https://archive.org/details/dinglers-polytechnisches-journal-vol-336/page/n399 }}</ref>

Jahnke studied [[mathematics]] and [[physics]] at the [[University of Berlin]], where he graduated in 1886. In 1889 he received his doctorate from [[Martin-Luther-Universität Halle-Wittenberg]] under Albert Wangerin on the integration of first-order [[ordinary differential equations]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=37664|name=Eugen Jahnke}}.</ref> After that, he was a teacher at secondary schools in Berlin, where he simultaneously in 1901 taught at the ''Königlich Technische Hochschule Berlin'' (now [[TU Berlin]]) and in 1905 he became a professor at the Mining Academy in Berlin, which merged in 1916 with the ''Technische Hochschule''. In 1919 he became [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of that institution.<ref>About the author, from E. Jahnke, ''Vorlesungen ueber die Vektorenrechnung: Mit Anwendungen auf Geometrie, Mechanik und mathematische Physik'', Vero Verlag, 2014, {{ISBN|978-3956108617}}.</ref>

In 1900 Jahnke read a paper at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Paris.<ref>{{cite book|chapter=Nouveaux systèmes orthogonaux dérivées des fonctions thêta de deux arguments|title=Compte rendu du deuxième Congrès International des Mathématiciens tenu à Paris du 6 au 12 Aout 1900|pages=279–280|url=http://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=miun.aag4063.0000.001;view=1up;seq=287}}</ref> He was editor of the Archives of Mathematics and Physics and contributor to the Yearbook for the Progress of Mathematics. He wrote an early book on [[vector calculus]] but is now known primarily for his function tables, which first appeared in 1909.  This was also translated into English and was in print into the 1960s. {{ill|Fritz Emde|de}} (Professor of Electrical Engineering at the [[University of Stuttgart]]) contributed to later editions, as did others.

== Selected works ==
* Jahnke: ''Zur Integration von Differentialgleichungen erster Ordnung, in welchen die unabhängige Veränderliche explicite nicht vorkommt, durch eindeutige doppeltperiodische Funktionen'' (dissertation), 1889<ref>{{cite web |title=Albert Wangerin (1844-1933) |url=http://disk.mathematik.uni-halle.de/history/wangerin/index.html |website=Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg |accessdate=3 July 2018}}</ref>
* Jahnke: [https://archive.org/details/vorlesungenberd00jahngoog ''Vorlesungen über die Vektorenrechnung – mit Anwendungen auf Geometrie, Mechanik und mathematische Physik''] (lectures on vector analysis, with applications to geometry, mechanics, and mathematical physics), Teubner 1905<ref>{{cite journal|author=Wilson, Edwin Bidwell|authorlink=Edwin Bidwell Wilson|title=Review: ''Vorlesungen über die Vektorenrechnung'' by Eugen Jahnke|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1906|issue=7|pages=352–356|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1906-12-07/S0002-9904-1906-01350-7/S0002-9904-1906-01350-7.pdf|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1906-01350-7|volume=12|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* {{anchor|JE}}Jahnke (jointly with {{ill|Fritz Emde|de}}): ''Funktionentafeln mit Formeln und Kurven'' (tables of functions with formulas and graphs), Teubner. 1909,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Wilson, Edwin Bidwell|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1911-17-07/S0002-9904-1911-02073-0/S0002-9904-1911-02073-0.pdf|title=Review of ''Einführung in die Theorie des Magnetismus'' by R. Gans; ''Einführung in die Maxwellsche Theorie der Elehtrizität und des Magnetismus'' by Cl. Schaefer; and ''Funktionentafeln mit Formeln und Kurven'' by E. Jahnke and F. Emde. Leipzig, Teubner, 1909. xii + 176 pp.|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1911|volume=17|issue=7|pages=350–361|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1911-02073-0|doi-access=free}}</ref> 1933, 1945, 7. Auflage 1966, edited by Fritz Emde until his death in 1951 and later by Friedrich Lösch as "Tafeln höherer Funktionen". In America, published as [https://archive.org/details/tablesoffunction00jahn ''Tables of Functions With Formulas and Curves''] by Eugene Jahnke and Fritz Emde, Dover June 1945
